questions.prompt: What does the Layout Service return for a selected item?

choices.text: JSON for the context, the route, and the placeholders
Finished HTML from the rendering engine
A Razor view compiled on the CD
Only the dictionary phrases for the language

questions.explain: The Layout Service outputs JSON based on the item's presentation details. The rendering engine is the path that still produces HTML.

questions.prompt: Which three parts are in a Layout Service response?

choices.text: Sitecore context, route, and placeholders with components
Templates, workflows, and security roles
Hosts file, IIS binding, and API key
GraphQL schema, mocks, and a WebSocket

questions.explain: Context holds language, pageEditing, and site info. The route holds the resolved item and its fields. Placeholders say which component goes where, with that component's data.

questions.prompt: In a Layout Service URL, what is sc_lang?

choices.text: The language
The item path
The API key item ID
The placeholder key

questions.explain: item is the path, sc_lang is the language, and sc_apikey is the API key item ID.

questions.prompt: What is the Dictionary Service for?

choices.text: Labels and fixed text on components
The hero title an author changes per campaign
The placeholder tree for the route
The IIS bindings for the app hostname

questions.explain: Dictionary phrases are fixed labels. A headline marketing changes is a field on a datasource.

questions.prompt: Where does an integrated GraphQL query run?

choices.text: In-process, inside the Layout Service, reshaping that rendering's data
In the browser, as an HTTP call started by Apollo
Only in disconnected mode, against a mock server
On the Content Delivery role as a Razor rendering

questions.explain: Integrated GraphQL is configured on the component and executed by the Layout Service. Connected GraphQL is the client request.

questions.prompt: What does connected GraphQL query?

choices.text: Your GraphQL endpoint, instead of changing the Layout Service output
The Component GraphQL Query field, with no front-end code
The dictionary file under /data/dictionary
The hosts file on the Sitecore server

questions.explain: Connected GraphQL is an HTTP or WebSocket request from the client. JSS integrates it with Apollo through GraphQLData.

questions.prompt: How is a GraphQL datasource field different from item?

choices.text: datasource goes through the parseDataSource pipeline, the way MVC resolves a datasource
item runs submit actions and datasource only returns dictionary phrases
They are the same field with two names
datasource is only available in disconnected mode

questions.explain: item retrieves the item. datasource resolves the value the same way a rendering datasource is resolved in MVC.

questions.prompt: How do you open the GraphQL UI for an app endpoint?

choices.text: Append /ui?sc_apikey=[your API key] to the endpoint
Open /sitecore/shell and choose Graph Browser from the ribbon
Run jss deploy config and read the terminal
Add tracking=false to the Layout Service URL

questions.explain: The workshop UI is http://ex.sitecore-jss-workshop.sc/api/exercises/ui with the API key.

questions.prompt: What is the editor difference between a parameters template and params: ["heading"]?

choices.text: A parameters template gives the author a field. A bare name list is a string a developer remembers
A bare name list is the only form Sitecore stores
They produce the same Experience Editor controls
params replaces the component fields

questions.explain: Parameters configure the component and are defined on the manifest. The template is what the author sees.

questions.prompt: What do you set on a Placeholder Settings item?

choices.text: The placeholder key, the allowed controls, and whether it is editable
CORS origins, AllowedControllers, and the impersonation user
The rendering host URL and the editing host URL
The dictionary language and the phrase list

questions.explain: Placeholder Settings live under Presentation. The key must match the name used in the app.

questions.prompt: Which way of starting can move to the other?

choices.text: Code-first can move to Sitecore-first. The reverse is not the path
Sitecore-first can be exported back into disconnected YAML at any time
Both directions are the same import
Neither can change after the first deploy

questions.explain: Code-first generates Sitecore artifacts on import. Sitecore-first leaves those artifacts to the Sitecore developer.

questions.prompt: What does jss start do?

choices.text: Runs the app in disconnected mode against local JSON and YAML
Deploys config files into the Sitecore App_Config folder
Imports the manifest and opens Experience Editor
Renders the site through Node on the Content Delivery server

questions.explain: Disconnected mode is a development mode. The browser renders, and the data is local. Connected mode is jss start:connected.

questions.prompt: Which modes are the production set?

choices.text: Integrated, API-only, and headless SSR. Integrated is also used while building
Disconnected and connected only
API-only is development, and disconnected is production
Headless SSR cannot run against a Sitecore CD

questions.explain: Development is disconnected, connected, and integrated while you build. Production is integrated, API-only, and headless SSR.

questions.prompt: What does jss deploy config do?

choices.text: Copies the app's Sitecore config files onto the Sitecore instance
Creates a production JS bundle and imports content items
Opens the GraphQL UI
Writes the hosts file and the IIS binding

questions.explain: jss deploy app is the build and the manifest import. jss deploy config is only the config files.

questions.prompt: What does jss deploy app --includeContent --includeDictionary do?

choices.text: Builds the app, imports content and dictionary items, and the app appears under /content
Only copies config into App_Config\Include
Starts disconnected mode on localhost:3000
Disables page-view tracking

questions.explain: After that import you can run integrated mode with Sitecore content, and you can run connected mode.

questions.prompt: Where do you create the API key item?

choices.text: /sitecore/system/Settings/Services/API Keys in the master database
/sitecore/content/home
/sitecore/layout/Renderings
/sitecore/templates/Project

questions.explain: Set CORS Origins and AllowedControllers on that item. Wildcards are for this training. Production needs real values.

questions.prompt: How do JSS and SXA split the work?

choices.text: SXA owns the site skeleton. JSS is the front end that renders each component
You pick one. A site cannot use both
SXA is the React SDK and JSS is the toolbox
JSS replaces placeholder settings, page designs, and shared content

questions.explain: JSS or SXA is the wrong question for a rebuild. They are used together.

questions.prompt: Which option adds a client library and decoupled rendering?

choices.text: JavaScript Services
Services Client only
Experience Accelerator only
None of them. All three stop at OData

questions.explain: Services Client, SXA, and JSS all return JSON and have security. Only JSS adds the client library and decoupled rendering.

questions.prompt: What is the Services Client?

choices.text: An OData item API
The React field helpers
The Node rendering host
The SXA toolbox

questions.explain: SXA reuses components, layouts, and templates and adds a JSON content service. JSS is the SDK for the JavaScript application.

questions.prompt: What does server-side JavaScript rendering send to the browser first?

choices.text: HTML from Node, then the UI library updates the page
A blank page until Apollo finishes
Razor markup from the MVC rendering engine
Only the dictionary JSON

questions.explain: The browser sends an HTTP request to Node. Node returns HTML and JavaScript. Later updates stay in React, Angular, or Vue.

questions.prompt: What is the warning on the integrated topology?

choices.text: Node and the CD share CPU, and caching is all or nothing
Sitecore must sit on a public URL with no proxy
You cannot use the Layout Service
It is the only topology that scales Node and the CDs separately

questions.explain: Integrated mode is a good fit for an embedded JSS app. Headless hosting is the one that scales the Node tier and the CDs apart.

questions.prompt: How does JSS track page views by default?

choices.text: Through the Layout Service. Add tracking=false to turn that off
Through the tracking service, which is on by default
Only when you call the dictionary endpoint
Only in disconnected mode

questions.explain: That default is configurable on the dataApi object. The separate tracking service stays off until Sitecore.JSS.TrackerServiceEnabled is true.

questions.prompt: What does a tracked page view require?

choices.text: A Sitecore item ID. A route that is not an item can use a surrogate ID
Only the browser URL
A GraphQL mutation
The component to be open in Experience Editor

questions.explain: The call is trackingApi.trackEvent with pageId and url, from sitecore-jss-tracking.

questions.prompt: Where can you not use Sitecore Forms?

choices.text: Disconnected mode
Integrated mode
A multistep form posted back to Sitecore
Any JSS app

questions.explain: The Layout Service can return the form schema, the browser renders it, and the post runs the submit action on Sitecore. That path is not available while the app is disconnected.

questions.prompt: How can a JSS app log into Sitecore?

choices.text: The Services Client Authentication Service sets the .ASPXAUTH cookie. Test it in integrated mode because of CORS
Put the password in the Layout Service item query
Dictionary phrases carry the session
jss deploy config creates the logged-in user

questions.explain: The Layout Service already respects the logged-in user and Sitecore security. The authentication call is what sets the cookie.

questions.prompt: How does connected GraphQL run while the app is disconnected?

choices.text: A mock GraphQL server is registered and requests are proxied to it
The browser calls the Sitecore CD directly with no proxy
Integrated queries are stored in the hosts file
It cannot be attempted until the app is imported

questions.explain: The exercises app does this in disconnected-mode-proxy.js with createDisconnectedGraphqlService.

questions.prompt: Where are the default JavaScript Services app settings defined?

choices.text: Sitecore.JavaScriptServices.Apps.config. Your app config inherits them
The dictionary YAML for English
The placeholder key on the Home item
package.json dependencies only

questions.explain: Apps are registered under javaScriptServices/apps. Check /sitecore/config/[yourappname].config, including hostName.

questions.prompt: What do you publish to when the rendering host reads Experience Edge?

choices.text: A GraphQL delivery endpoint. A field change does not require a Node rebuild
The disconnected YAML files
A new MVC rendering for every field
The hosts file on each CD

questions.explain: Experience Edge is a publishing target for items, layout, and media. The rendering host reads the published layout.

questions.prompt: On the hero, what owns the HTML and what owns the field values?

choices.text: The React component owns the HTML. The layout document owns the field values
The dictionary owns both
The Razor view owns the HTML after the move to JSS
Search owns the hero template

questions.explain: Search can sit in a placeholder beside the hero. It is a separate component.

questions.prompt: In a coupled CMS, who emits the HTML?

choices.text: The Content Delivery role, as part of the same application that stores the content
A separate Node rendering host
The browser, from Layout Service JSON only
Experience Edge

questions.explain: Coupled means content management, delivery, and presentation are one web application. A new channel repeats that presentation.

questions.prompt: What is JSS for a JavaScript developer?

choices.text: A complete SDK for building the application with modern UI libraries, including modern rendering
A replacement for the SXA site skeleton
An OData item browser with no UI helpers
A hosts-file editor

questions.explain: The libraries supply placeholder and field components. The same idea is published for React, React Native, Angular, and Vue.

questions.prompt: What must match between the React layout and Sitecore?

choices.text: The placeholder name, such as jss-main
The dictionary phrase for Documentation
The deployment secret and the page title
The GraphQL mock return value

questions.explain: The layout renders that placeholder, the manifest registers it, and package.json lists it in rootPlaceholders. Sitecore will not return a placeholder the component did not register.
